assessments.reasoning: LaTeX Project 1.3c original, acquisition f8dfb3a74daa4a65bc6a79cd6cdcde04. Connector range [5345,18225), SHA-256 d4fc9f7eeb914307da183028e1d8d5cfb3ea1068b71fb6c180bd894f98609bf3, includes both the operative clause and the later non-replacement passage. Reading both supports the conditional modality and identifies a concrete case outside its scope.

challenge.method: Read clause 6(d) together with the later section “Derived Works That Are Not Replacements.” Tested reuse of a few lines for a completely different task, a Current Maintainer distribution, a component exemption, equivalent access, compiled distribution and a different license.
challenge.results: For a Derived Work unintended as a compatible or incompatible replacement, the later passage expressly disapplies both 6(b) and 6(d). This defeats an unconditional claim and fits the candidate’s applicability condition. Only the Current Maintainer may add a clear component copyright-notice exemption from a particular condition. Where 6(d) applies, equivalent access from the same or a similar place can satisfy the copy option in the designated-place case. Clause 7 incorporates clause 6 for the underlying Derived Work, and 10(a) requires an alternative license to honor applicable clause 6 conditions regarding the Work.

limitations: Application depends on the distributor’s maintainer status, condition-specific component exemptions and whether the Derived Work is intended as a replacement. A particular work’s status, intended use and compliance were outside the review.
reasoning: Where 1.3c clause 6(d) applies, its two alternatives require the distributor to provide with the Derived Work at least one of a complete unmodified copy of the Work or information sufficient to obtain one. The candidate expressly conditions the obligation on 6(d) applying.
